one_liner: Freshdesk has a broad REST v2 API that most likely uses per-agent API keys (Basic key:X). The supplied pages confirm a trial with a 50 calls/min API limit, and the vendor's own site promotes a Freshdesk MCP integration.
auth_notes: The supplied pages never show the Freshdesk REST authentication section. The only nearby evidence is the Freshworks credential-store page, which says Freshservice API keys work as Basic auth with the key as username and "x" as password. That is a sibling product, so Freshdesk's key:X scheme is inferred from it and from general knowledge. A third-party blog (rollout.com) describes an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow against Freshdesk, but it is not vendor documentation and I did not rely on it. OAuth pages in the SDK docs cover OAuth for marketplace apps calling third parties, not Freshdesk's own API. Composio lists API_KEY only. Auth is low confidence.
access_notes: The API page confirms the API works in a trial, with a default limit of 50 calls/minute. Rate limits are listed per paid plan. The homepage offers "Start for free", but the pages don't say whether a free plan includes API access. Access stays at self_serve_trial with reduced confidence.
blocker_notes: Development works in a trial (50 calls/min). Ongoing use needs a paid plan, because rate limits are tied to paid plans and are account-wide. Each customer must supply their own subdomain and API key. The pages don't confirm whether a free plan includes API access.
